data.title: Australian employment falls sharply in October, jobless hits 4.9%
data.description:
Australian employment fell for a second straight month in October, while the jobless rate climbed to a fresh five-year high, a surprisingly soft result that bolstered the case interest rates have likely reached their peak.

Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed net employment fell 43,500 in October from September, when it dropped 36,400. Analysts had forecast a rise of around 25,000.

The jobless rate climbed to 4.9%, the highest since October 2021, from 4.7% a month ago. The participation rate dipped to 66.6%, while hours worked fell 0.2%.

data.title: KPMG Canada confirms cyber incident, unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents
data.description:
KPMG Canada confirmed on Wednesday a third party gained unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents in a cybersecurity incident.

The firm did not disclose how many clients were affected, how many files were compromised or how the breach occurred.

KPMG has secured its systems and is contacting affected clients, spokesperson Sonja Cloutier-Bosworth said.

"We are confident we have protected our clients' information and, based on our ongoing monitoring, the information impacted by this incident is not available online or being misused for any purpose," Cloutier-Bosworth said.

The Globe and Mail first reported the news earlier in the day.

The incident comes amid heightened cyber risks for professional-service and financial firms that hold sensitive client information. Recent attacks have targeted law firms, private equity firms and other financial companies.

data.title: Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show
data.description:
A few Federal Reserve officials who supported holding interest rates steady in October considered the decision a “close call,” according to minutes released Wednesday, as policymakers signaled that further hikes would likely be needed to bring inflation back to 2%.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10–2 in October to keep its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored a quarter-point increase. The minutes showed that a few participants who supported holding rates steady still viewed the decision as a “close call.”

“The minutes suggest broader support for an October hike than the 10–2 vote alone implied — and that was before payrolls and CPI both came in hot,” Lewis Huang, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitget, told Cointelegraph.

With markets overwhelmingly expecting a December rate hike, attention is shifting to whether the Fed will raise rates by a quarter or half percentage point.

“With a December hike already fully priced in, the focus shifts to the size of the move and the policy path beyond December,” said Huang.

CME FedWatch has put the odds of a December quarter-point hike at about 90% and a half-point increase at about 10% at the time of writing.

Bitcoin was trading around $62,300 after the minutes were released. Huang said a further rise in Treasury yields and the dollar would add pressure to Bitcoin, which was already trading below its 200-week moving average near $68,000.

“For Bitcoin, a break below the weekend low near $62,000 could extend the sell-off,” Huang said.

Fed officials flag AI inflation and financial stability risks

Fed officials also raised concerns about the inflationary impact of AI investment, with many participants noting that demand for related equipment was straining supply and pushing up consumer technology prices. Several warned that the pressures were spreading beyond industries directly involved in data center construction.

Officials separately discussed the financial risks if AI investments disappointed.

“Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures,” the minutes show. “A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms.”

Fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank, said markets were already pricing in a series of hikes into next year.

“That likely keeps long-term yields and the dollar firm, and the question for Bitcoin is whether debasement concerns and advancing institutional adoption can outweigh it,” Dori said.

data.title: Future Metals Commences Copper-Nickel-PGM Exploration at Eileen Bore Target
data.description:
Future Metals has commenced on-ground exploration at the Eileen Bore copper target and across its broader Alice Downs Corridor (ADC) tenements in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia.

An ongoing review of historical and recent datasets by independent consultant Resource Potentials has identified several near-term copper-nickel-gold-platinum group metals (PGM) areas of focus close to the Eileen Bore Main (EB-Main) exploration target.

The scope of work will focus on the new Eileen Bore-T1 (EB-T1) area immediately north of EB-Main, which has previously shown coincident gravity, electromagnetic and magnetic anomalies.

It will also investigate a series of untested downhole electromagnetic conductors (DHEM) at EB-Main identified in the review from historical drilling and surveying.

Further exploration across the mafic-ultramafic intrusive ADC will include soil sampling and drone magnetic surveying to identify and refine additional copper-nickel-PGM targets.

Progressive Exploration

Future’s exploration program will be progressed in stages including soil geochemistry, a drone magnetic survey, geological and geophysical integration, geological mapping, and a diamond drilling campaign.

The scope and timing of drilling activities remains subject to final drill design, regulatory approvals, heritage and land access requirements, as well as rig availability.

The planned campaign—which has received up to $88,250 in co-funding under Round 34 of the state government’s exploration incentive scheme—aims to build on the EB-Main exploration target of approximately 12 million tonnes to 15Mt grading 0.35% to 0.45% copper, 0.15% to 0.22% nickel, and 0.1 grams per tonne to 0.15g/t gold (0.62% to 0.86% CuEq).

Exploration results will inform a 2027 work program aimed at defining a maiden copper equivalent mineral resource estimate at ADC.

Historical Prospective Corridor

The prospective ADC extends over 18 kilometres within the Halls Creek Orogen, located around 20km east of Future’s Panton PGM project.

It is characterised by multiple gravity-defined intrusions emplaced adjacent to the regional-scale Alice Downs Fault, interpreted to represent a splay-off of the broader crustal-scale Halls Creek Fault system.

Historical exploration largely focused on multiple generations of smaller surveys that produced surface geochemistry and discrete EM anomalies, with limited systematic integration of broader geological and geophysical datasets.

Resource Potentials’ ongoing review comprises historical and recent exploration datasets including a detailed ground gravity survey, moving loop, airborne and ground EM surveys, DHEM data, and available drilling information.

Future is looking to improve its geological understanding of the Eileen Bore complex, reassess historical results, and identify opportunities for further exploration program across the broader ADC.

Strong Momentum Building

Managing director Keith Bowes said the company was building strong momentum at new exploration targets within Eileen Bore and the ADC.

“A key focus for us is EB-T1, immediately north of EB-Main, where coincident gravity, EM, and magnetic anomalies present a compelling opportunity for follow-up drilling,” he said.

“Together with an untested EM conductor targeting base metal sulphide minerals south of EB-Main, we now have clear priorities to develop a drilling program that we can execute next year with the aim of producing our first mineral resource estimate.”

Heritage approvals have been secured, and the company has commenced geochemical soil sampling and high-resolution drone magnetic surveying to sharpen its targeting efforts and guide future drilling.

data.title: Teams of Weil lawyers join rival firms as wind-down accelerates
data.description:
By David Thomas

Major US law firms are continuing to scoop up lawyers from Weil, Gotshal & Manges, including more than two dozen new partner hires by Skadden, Sidley Austin, Simpson Thacher, Dechert and Kirkland & Ellis.

Weil ​lawyers are scattering following the New York firm’s decision this month to wind down operations, boosting partnerships at its onetime competitors. Partners at Weil voted last week to dissolve the firm after mounting departures, cementing the fall of a 95-year-old law firm that helped steer high-profile bankruptcies, corporate takeovers and litigation for decades.

The moves ​add to an already busy hiring market for law firms that's been supercharged by Weil's collapse. Earlier this week Cleary Gottlieb, Paul Hastings and Skadden said they were bringing on other lawyers from Weil.

Skadden said on Wednesday it was adding a team of 11 restructuring partners as well as seven intellectual property partners from Weil. Matt Barr, who led Weil's vaunted restructuring practice, will become the head of Skadden's global restructuring group, the firm said, with about 40 Weil restructuring and corporate attorneys joining in all.

Among the IP litigators moving to Skadden are Douglas Lumish and Jeff Homrig, who co-led the firm's IP, technology & science litigation group. Lumish and Homrig will co-lead Skadden's IP litigation group.

Sidley on Wednesday said it hired 14 partners from Weil, including its M&A head and corporate department co-chair Michael Lubowitz, US private equity practice co-head Peter Feist, corporate co-managing partner Lyuba Goltser, banking and finance co-head Andrew Colao, tech and IP transactions head Charan Sandhu, and US privacy and cybersecurity head Olivia Greer.

The group includes more than 35 lawyers, according to Sidley, which Reuters earlier reported was in talks to hire around 200 people from Weil, including lawyers and staff members.

Simpson Thacher said it was adding five Weil partners to its ranks, including John Barry, who led its employment practice. Barry will now lead Simpson Thacher's employment practice, the firm said.

Dechert said it hired corporate partner Nandan Nelivigi and tax partner Michael Sykes from Weil. Nelivigi works on deals involving major energy and infrastructure projects, while Sykes advises on tax incentives and financing strategies for energy projects, Dechert said.

Kirkland said Weil tax partner Lauren Gorsche will be joining the firm.

Weil's decision to wind down has forced a scramble among both its lawyers and non-attorney staffers. In California, the firm said it will be eliminating more than 100 jobs, according to a series of Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (WARN) notices filed with the state.

data.title: Elon Musk Says Nvidia Ousting Jensen Huang Is Like Kicking Michael Jordan Off A Winning Team
data.description:
Key points:
  • When asked if he sees Huang returning to Nvidia, Musk said that it is ultimately on Nvidia’s board of directors or shareholders.
  • “…there's no one that can really replace Jensen,” Musk said.
  • Musk’s companies and Nvidia share deep business ties.

Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday criticized Nvidia’s board’s decision to oust Jensen Huang as CEO, calling it “like kicking Michael Jordan off of your team when you are on a winning streak .”

“I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said about the former Nvidia CEO who was ousted after reports of romantic relations with a Chinese intelligence asset.

Musk described Huang as “an old friend of mine” and added that the board’s decision to oust him “doesn't seem like a smart decision to me.”

“…there's no one that can really replace Jensen,” Musk said at The New York Times Dealbook Summit. “He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades. He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him, loves him, and many of them are there because of him, and have had higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.”

Will Huang Return To Nvidia?

When asked if he sees Huang returning to Nvidia, Musk said that it is ultimately on Nvidia’s board of directors or shareholders. “I think, like the current board would either need to change their mind, or shareholders would need to vote the board out at the shareholders meeting, which is that's that's pretty rare for that to happen. So, but really the board is in charge of the company right now,” the Tesla CEO said.

Earlier this week, Nvidia's board chairman firmly stated during the earnings call that Jensen Huang will not be reinstated under any circumstances. Earlier today, it was also reported that a recruitment agency hired by Nvidia’s (NVDA) board has reportedly officially reached out to Arm Holdings (ARM) CEO Rene Haas to take over the reins at the chipmaker.

Musk Companies And Nvidia 

Musk’s companies and Nvidia share deep business ties. SpaceX has publicly committed to building its expanding AI infrastructure, including terrestrial data centers and planned orbital computing, exclusively on Nvidia’s platforms, with Musk describing the Vera Rubin architecture as the best available and stating that the company expects to receive a significant share of Nvidia’s GPU output. Nvidia also holds a stake in SpaceX.

Musk’s EV company Tesla, meanwhile, relies on Nvidia hardware for AI training even as it develops its own inference chips for Full Self-Driving and the Optimus robot.

Talking about his own comments about wanting to hire Huang at the Summit, Musk asked, “Who wouldn't want to hire Jensen?”

How Did TSLA, SPCX Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA and SPCX was within the 'bullish' territory at the time of writing.

While TSLA stock has slipped 15% year-to-date, SPCX stock is currently trading at about $143.5, above its June IPO price of $135. Nvidia, meanwhile, clocked its fifth consecutive day in the red on Wednesday and is down 19% this year.

data.title: Immutep Reports Encouraging Disease-Free Survival from EFTISARC-NEO Phase II Trial in Soft Tissue Sarcoma
data.description:
Key points:
  • Poster presented today at CTOS 2026 expands on the survival data first reported in the abstract (announced 11 November 2026), which showed a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% in patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma.
  • Patients with post-treatment tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels.
  • Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels.
  • Results build on previously reported strong pathological responses and further support the potential of efti-based combination therapy.

SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Immutep Limited (ASX: IMM; NASDAQ: IMMP) (“Immutep” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel LAG-3 immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune diseases, today announced new data from the investigator-initiated EFTISARC-NEO Phase II study presented at the Connective Tissue Oncology Society (CTOS) 2026 Annual Meeting (Poster number P 448).

The study is evaluating Immutep’s eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy before surgery in patients with high-risk, resectable soft tissue sarcoma. Forty patients were enrolled, and 38 patients underwent surgery and were included in the survival evaluation.

The latest analysis currently shows a disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% at 12 months. The current Kaplan-Meier estimate at 18 months is also 81.1%, although this later time point remains immature, and follow-up is ongoing. Among the 38 patients who underwent surgery and were evaluated, eight patients had experienced disease recurrence at the data cut-off (April 30, 2026).

Table 1 – Survival results for soft tissue sarcoma patients from EFTISARC-NEO

OutcomeLatest Analysis
12-month disease-free survival (mature)81.1%
18-month disease-free survival (immature)81.1%
12-month local recurrence-free survival94.1%
12-month distant metastasis-free survival86.2%
Median follow-up19.1 months

In addition, exploratory analyses showed that higher levels of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and greater hyalinisation and fibrosis after treatment may be associated with better DFS. In particular, patients with post-treatment TIL levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels. Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels of hyalinisation and fibrosis. The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and baseline expression of PD-L1, LAG-3 and TIGIT did not correlate with survival outcomes.

These survival and exploratory findings build on previously reported EFTISARC-NEO results in which the trial met its primary endpoint with a median tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis of 51.5% following neoadjuvant therapy with efti, pembrolizumab and radiotherapy. The new data are consistent with efti's mechanism of action, in which activation of antigen-presenting cells drives a stronger anti-tumour T cell response, and suggest that a stronger immune response in the tumour may be associated with improved patient survival outcomes.

Pawel Sobczuk, MD PhD, one of the Principal Investigators of EFTISARC-NEO, said: “These results are highly encouraging for patients with high-risk soft tissue sarcoma, where recurrence remains a major concern despite surgery and radiotherapy. Disease-free survival of approximately 81% maintained through 12 months and on a preliminary basis also at 18 months is an important observation, and the association between a strong immune response in the tumour and better disease-free survival is particularly compelling. Together with the substantial pathological responses previously reported, the findings reinforce the potential of this novel neoadjuvant approach and provide a strong rationale for continued follow-up and further clinical evaluation.”

Marc Voigt, CEO of Immutep, said: “With the data to date, EFTISARC-NEO is delivering an increasingly coherent and encouraging picture. The marked difference in outcomes between patients with higher and lower post-treatment immune cell infiltration is especially notable and is consistent with efti’s potential to help generate a stronger anti-tumour immune response. We believe these results strengthen the rationale for further potential clinical development in this indication, where patients remain in need of more effective treatment options.”

The poster is available on the Posters & Publications page of Immutep’s website.

Next Steps

Immutep anticipates reporting additional data from EFTISARC-NEO in CY2027.

Subject to regulatory interactions, manufacturing timelines, partnering arrangements and available resources, the Company is preparing to advance efti into a registration-directed clinical trial in neoadjuvant soft tissue sarcoma, targeting initiation in H2 CY2027.

About EFTISARC-NEO

EFTISARC-NEO is an investigator-initiated, open-label Phase II trial evaluating eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment for patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma. The trial is led by the Maria Skłodowska-Curie National Research Institute of Oncology in Warsaw, Poland, and is primarily funded by a grant from the Polish Medical Research Agency, with Immutep supplying efti.

The primary endpoint is pathological response, measured as the percentage of tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis at resection. Secondary endpoints include safety, disease-free survival, local recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, radiological response and health-related quality of life. Forty patients were enrolled, with enrolment completed in January 2025 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128863).

About Eftilagimod Alfa (efti)

Eftilagimod alfa (efti) is Immutep’s proprietary soluble LAG-3 protein and MHC Class II agonist that activates antigen-presenting cells through the MHC Class II pathway, engaging both innate and adaptive immunity, including the priming of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and the production of co-stimulatory signals and cytokines. Its favourable safety profile enables combination with anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Efti has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and first-line non-small cell lung cancer, and Orphan Drug Designation in soft tissue sarcoma.

About Immutep

Immutep is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. The Company is a pioneer in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3), and its diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s ability to stimulate or suppress the immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximise value for shareholders. For more information, please visit www.immutep.com.

data.description:
Key points:
  • Poster presented today at CTOS 2026 expands on the survival data first reported in the abstract (announced 11 November 2026), which showed a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% in patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma.
  • Patients with post-treatment tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels.
  • Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels.
  • Results build on previously reported strong pathological responses and further support the potential of efti-based combination therapy.

Immutep reported 81.1% disease-free survival at 12 months in EFTISARC-NEO; the 18-month Kaplan-Meier estimate is also 81.1% but remains immature. Eight of 38 patients evaluated had recurrence by April 30, 2026.

data.title: Anthropic Officially Prices Its IPO At $83 A Share In $81.3B Debut, Shattering IPO Records
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised $81.3 billion across 980 million shares, surpassing SpaceX’s previous all-time IPO record.
  • Orders for the offering outpaced available shares by nearly seven times despite a broader tech market downturn.
  • The Claude developer is set to debut on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ‘ANT’.

Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share Wednesday evening, in the largest public market debut in history with a valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion.

Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised a combined $81.3 billion through the upsized sale of 980 million shares of Class A common stock compared to the previously marketed range of $70 to $78 per share.

The offering, which includes a $26 billion private placement, eclipsed the previous global IPO record set by SpaceX. Including its over-allotment option, SpaceX had raised $86.2 billion.

Structure of the Offering

Anthropic directly sold 956.35 million shares, while certain selling stockholders—specifically the company's co-founders—offloaded 23.65 million shares. Anthropic stated it will not collect any financial proceeds from the shares sold by its co-founders.

Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC spearheaded the underwriting syndicate alongside 20 additional financial institutions. Shares are scheduled to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ‘ANT’.

Heavy Demand Defies Tech Slump

Orders for Anthropic’s shares reached nearly seven times the available supply, drawing heavy interest from global financial hubs including New York, London and Tokyo.

Because demand far exceeded supply, bankers notified prospective buyers that existing backers would receive priority allocations, leaving some new investors with smaller stakes than requested, Bloomberg reported.

The robust appetite materialized despite broader headwinds in the technology sector. The Nasdaq 100 Index fell 4.4% over the week leading up to Wednesday's market close, while chipmaker Nvidia Corp. saw its stock decline 2.9% Wednesday for a fifth consecutive losing session. Notably, Nvidia is set to acquire $10 billion worth of Anthropic stock through the offering's private placement component.

Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) share prices also rose after-hours. Both companies own sizable chunks of Anthropic.

Microsoft (MSFT), Salesforce (CRM) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) are among other large tech companies that have invested in Anthropic.

Where Does Anthropic Stand?

Anthropic has now become the first AI lab to list on a public exchange, beating primary rival OpenAI, which is not expected to pursue a public listing before 2027.

At a $1.5 trillion valuation, Anthropic immediately ranks among the 15 largest publicly traded companies globally, standing roughly on par with Tesla Inc.(TSLA).

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits towards Anthropic was ‘extremely bullish’ ahead of its official pricing, with ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

data.title: JGBs Edge Higher Amid Mixed Developments — Market Talk
data.description: JGBs edge higher in price terms in Tokyo's morning session amid mixed developments. On the one hand, JGBs are likely to be underpinned by the Bank of Japan's planned outright purchases today of three sectors of Japan's government bond market such as sovereign securities with tenors of more than five years and up to 10 years. Another market-supportive factor is lower oil prices that tend to ease inflationary pressure in Japan. On the other hand, however, investors might adopt a cautious stance amid substantial volatility in yields, market observers say. The 10-year JGB yield is down 1 bp at 2.860%. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: Japan Or Machinery Orders Sink 0.3% In September
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - The value of core machinery orders in Japan was down a seasonally adjusted 0.3 percent on month in September, the Cabinet Office said on Thursday - coming in at 1,066.2 billion yen.

That was shy of expectations for an increase of 1.3 percent following the 5.2 percent gain in August.

On a yearly basis, orders rose 13.4 percent - again missing expectations for 13/7 percent and down from 18.6 percent in the previous month.

For the third quarter of 2026, orders were up 1.2 percent on quarter and 14.1 percent on year at 3,152.8 billion yen.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, orders re forecast to rise 4.3 percent on quarter and 13.9 percent on year to 3,287.0 billion yen.

data.title: Oil Falls, Weighed by Larger-Than-Expected Rise in U.S. Inventories — Market Talk
data.description: Oil falls in early Asian trade. U.S. crude oil inventories rose more than expected in a second straight weekly build, according to data released Wednesday by the EIA. Commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve increased by 3.4 million barrels in the week ended Nov. 13, the data showed. data.title: Australia shares extend losses as miners slide; jobs data in focus
data.description:
Australian shares edged lower on Thursday, on track for a sixth consecutive day of losses as miners extended their slide on persistent weakness in copper prices, while investors awaited domestic employment data due later in the day.

The S&P/ASX 200 index was down 0.9% at 8,821.80 points, as of 2300 GMT. The benchmark closed 0.7% lower on Wednesday.

Miners declined 3.5% to their weakest level since late March as copper prices slumped to a seven-month low.

The sub-index has shed roughly 14% over the past few sessions despite a mild recovery in iron ore futures in the previous session.

Shares of BHP fell 3.8% to an early-April low on Thursday, while Rio Tinto hovered near its weakest level since last December.

Gold stocks shed 3.6% as hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve pushed gold to a 14-month low, reinforcing expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer.

Shares of Northern Star Resources and Evolution Mining were down 3% each.

Meanwhile, banks retreated 0.2%, putting the sub-index on track for a third consecutive session of losses.

National Australia Bank and Macquarie fell 0.6% each, outweighing modest gains in the other major lenders.

Australia's October employment data is due at 0030 GMT and will be closely scrutinised for clues on whether labour market conditions remain a source of concern for the Reserve Bank of Australia.

Last month, RBA Governor Michele Bullock said that the labour market continued to be tighter than the central bank had previously assessed and that a further period of economic growth would be needed to bring sticky inflation back under control.

Technology stocks fell 0.3% despite overnight gains on the tech-heavy Nasdaq after chipmaker Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above estimates.

Shares of Xero fell 0.5%.

Farther south-east, New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 0.2% to 14,264.29 points.
